who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), test selection lane, fix-hello-1113
where: crates/blaze-api/src/lib.rs TestResult, TestsOf; crates/blaze-api/src/borrowed.rs TestResultRef; crates/blaze-api/src/frames/identity.rs
what: A field added to TestResult (`not_kept`) was declared after `executable`; the deterministic CBOR codec writes fields in declaration order and requires that order to be the canonical one (shorter key first, then bytewise), so the struct encoded in a non-canonical order and only the identity test over every response would have caught it.
cost: a pass of the lane reordering the owned and the borrowed struct by hand, with nothing compiled to say which was wrong
cause: the wire order is implied by the Rust declaration order and checked only by a byte-identity test, not where the struct is written
class: a persisted or wire layout that a source-level reorder changes silently: the order of declaration is a format decision nobody sees as one
prevention: a derive-time (reflection) check that every API struct's fields are declared in canonical CBOR key order, failing to compile with the field named; until then the identity test is the only guard
workaround: declare fields by encoded key length, then bytewise, in both the owned and the borrowed struct
fix: reordered by hand in the working tree of fix-hello-1113; the compile-time check is not built
